text: Given a directory containing a file whose name embeds U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE, such as "Screenshot 2026-01-14 at 3.42.11 PM.png", the renamer includes that file in its candidate set.

A file whose Spotlight attribute kMDItemIsScreenCapture is true is included in the candidate set even when its filename does not begin with "Screenshot", for example a German-locale "Bildschirmfoto" capture or a capture the user already renamed by hand.

An image file that neither carries a true kMDItemIsScreenCapture attribute nor matches the screenshot filename pattern is excluded from the candidate set, and is included when the --all-images flag is passed.
Enumeration of the target directory is non-recursive by default and descends into subdirectories only when --recursive is passed.
When --recursive is passed, symbolic links to directories are not followed and no file is visited more than once.
A file with SF_DATALESS set in its stat.st_flags is skipped without being opened or read, and the run report states how many such files were skipped along with their total nominal size in bytes.
When --materialize is passed, files with SF_DATALESS set are read and processed like any other candidate rather than being skipped.
A file whose image format is outside JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP is excluded from the candidate set and a per-file exclusion reason is recorded in the plan output.
Peak resident memory does not grow proportionally with corpus size: a run over 50,000 candidate files uses no more than twice the peak resident memory of a run over 500 candidate files.
Every filename the renamer proposes matches the regular expression ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z0-9]+$.

The date prefix of a proposed filename is the capture date parsed from the original filename when that filename is parseable, and otherwise the file's st_birthtime, rendered as YYYY-MM-DD in the machine's local timezone.
Given a stubbed model that returns the text "3:42 PM / dashboard", the proposed filename contains neither a forward slash nor a colon.
Every proposed filename is at most 255 bytes long when encoded as UTF-8, counting its extension.
When a proposed filename must be shortened to fit the 255-byte limit, the truncation occurs at a kebab-segment boundary rather than mid-segment, and the truncated name never ends with a hyphen.
No proposed filename begins with a period or a hyphen, and none ends with a space or a period.

The original file extension is preserved and lowercased so that a file named with .PNG becomes .png, and the file's content hash is unchanged after the rename, proving the image bytes were not re-encoded.
Non-ASCII text coming from OCR or from the model is transliterated to ASCII before slugification, and any character with no transliteration is dropped rather than emitted raw into the filename.
Two separate runs over the same image bytes with the same model identifier and the same prompt-template version produce byte-identical proposed filenames.

For a screenshot of a Slack thread discussing a Stripe outage, the slug segment immediately following the date prefix is the application, producing a name of the form 2026-01-14-slack-stripe-outage-thread.png rather than 2026-01-14-stripe-outage-slack-thread.png.
Application names are canonicalized through an alias map stored as a data file before slugification, so that "Google Chrome", "Chrome", and "Chrome Canary" all yield the app token "chrome".
An application name absent from the alias map is slugified from the model-returned name unchanged, and the same input application name always yields the same token.
When no application can be identified in a capture, the proposed filename consists of the date prefix and subject segments only, with no placeholder segment such as "unknown" or "app".

When two different candidate files in one run would produce the same final filename, each final filename receives a six-hex-character suffix derived from that file's own content hash, for example 2026-01-14-terminal-output-a3f9c1.png.
Re-running the renamer over the same corpus produces the same disambiguation suffixes as the previous run.

A proposed filename "stripe-dashboard.png" is treated as colliding with an existing on-disk file named "Stripe-Dashboard.png", with the comparison performed case-folded and NFC-normalized, and is disambiguated instead of overwriting that file.
A proposed filename that matches a pre-existing file the renamer is not itself renaming is disambiguated rather than clobbering that file.
The set of inodes present in the target directory after a run with --apply is identical to the set present before it, so no run ever reduces or replaces files.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: A run without --apply leaves every candidate file's name, inode, mtime, and st_flags unchanged, verified by comparing a full directory snapshot taken before and after the run.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: A run without --apply writes a plan.jsonl file containing exactly one record per candidate file, each record carrying the fields path, content_hash, action, proposed_name, reason, ocr_char_count, and est_cost_usd.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: The action field of every plan record is exactly one of "rename", "abstain", "skip", or "error".

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: Files are renamed only when --apply is passed, and no environment variable, configuration file value, or built-in default causes renaming to occur without it.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: Before issuing any model request, the run prints an estimated total cost in USD for the files it intends to process.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: When --max-cost is set to a USD value and the pre-run estimate exceeds it, the renamer exits with a non-zero status before issuing any model request and renames nothing.

group: Dry run, plan output, and apply
text: Running with --apply and --plan pointing at a previously written plan file executes exactly the renames recorded in that plan and issues zero model requests.
For each rename, a JSONL record containing run_id, ts, old_path, new_path, and content_hash is appended and fsynced to the journal before the corresponding rename(2) call is issued.

When the process is killed by an injected fault between the journal write and the rename call, the journal contains the record while the file still has its original name, and a subsequent re-run reconciles this state without error.
The undo subcommand restores the most recent run's renames to their original filenames and prints the number of files restored.
The undo subcommand with --run-id set to an earlier run's identifier restores that specific run's renames rather than those of the most recent run.

The undo subcommand compares each file's current content hash against the hash recorded in the journal, leaves untouched any file whose contents changed since the rename, lists each such file in its output, and exits with a non-zero status.
The undo subcommand skips any journal entry whose original filename is now occupied by a different file, reports that entry, and does not overwrite the occupying file.
Re-running the renamer over a directory it has already renamed proposes zero renames, with each already-renamed file recorded as skipped with the reason "already_renamed".

After a SIGKILL during a run with --apply, re-invoking the identical command performs zero OCR operations and zero model requests for files completed in the interrupted run, and completes the remaining files.

The cache key for a model result includes the content hash, the model identifier, and the prompt-template version, so that changing the prompt template invalidates cached model output while cached OCR output for the same file is still reused.
A file whose OCR output is shorter than the --min-ocr-chars threshold (default 12) and whose image entropy is below the configured threshold is recorded with action "abstain" and is not renamed.
A file recorded with action "abstain" still has its original filename after a run with --apply completes.

A model refusal, signalled either by the provider's stop reason or by the refusal check applied to the response text, yields action "abstain" with reason "model_declined", the run continues, and the process exit code is unaffected by refusals alone.
A model response that fails schema validation is retried once, and a second validation failure records action "error" for that file while the run continues processing the remaining files.
No file recorded with action "abstain" or action "error" is renamed under any combination of command-line flags.

When reading the target directory raises EPERM, the renamer exits with code 3 and prints the System Settings path for granting Full Disk Access to the parent terminal application, emitting no stack trace on stdout or stderr.
When no API key is present in the environment and --local was not passed, the renamer exits with code 2 and a message naming the missing environment variable, before enumerating any files.

An HTTP 429 response triggers exponential backoff that honours the retry-after header, and a run against an injected 429-then-200 response sequence completes with no file recorded with action "error".

The number of simultaneous in-flight model requests never exceeds the configured concurrency limit (default 8, settable with --concurrency), asserted by an instrumented transport that records overlapping requests.
On SIGINT the renamer stops dispatching new work, allows in-flight renames to complete and be journalled, prints a partial summary, and exits with code 130.
A run interrupted by SIGINT resumes from where it stopped when the identical command is invoked again, without reprocessing files already completed.
With --local passed, the process opens no outbound network connection other than to the configured Ollama host, asserted by a socket-level hook in the test suite.
With --local passed and the configured Ollama host unreachable, the renamer exits with a non-zero status and a message naming that host, and renames nothing.
The cloud backend and the local backend are reached through the same interface, such that the identical pipeline test suite passes against both with only the backend selection flag changed.
After a run with --apply, each renamed file still carries its com.apple.metadata:kMDItemIsScreenCapture and com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags extended attributes.
After a run with --apply, each renamed file's mtime and st_birthtime are identical to their values before the run.

Passing --sample N processes a pseudo-random subset of exactly N candidate files chosen deterministically from the --seed value (which has a fixed default), so the same directory and seed always select the same files.
A run with --sample changes nothing on disk even when --apply is passed alongside it.

On completion the renamer prints a report containing counts for each action, the number of distinct proposed slugs versus the total number of renames, the count of slugs proposed more than once, and the minimum, median, and maximum proposed filename length.
The completion report includes 20 randomly sampled old-name-to-new-name pairs, or all pairs when fewer than 20 renames occurred.
Passing --prompt-template with a path uses the prompt at that path instead of the built-in one, and the --print-prompt flag writes the built-in prompt to stdout so it can be copied and edited.
